description: The New Zealand benefit unit (engine Family entity): an adult, their co-resident partner, and their dependent children; every other adult forms their own unit. The unit id family.family_id and the membership person.person_family_id are structural graph columns: the graph executor counts each entity's id column and each person-table membership column as structural (microcosm.graph.executor._structural_columns) and rejects a non-structural node that declares one as an output (microcosm.graph.executor._validate_population_declaration). family.family_household_id, the unit's link to its household, is not structural; it is an ordinary family column. The planned shared transport CREATE kernel (packages G4 and G5a) is to build the units from the donor concept pointers, refusing ambiguous or cross-household units. Family weights are never stored: each unit inherits its household's weight through the Frame.
status: awaiting D1 (MC7; the dependent-child rule is spec data under amendment MC11a, which is proposed and also awaits D1)

pointer_concepts.citation: microcosm.frame.concepts, the partner_person_id, parent_1_person_id, parent_2_person_id and reference_person_id pointer concepts

composition.rule: each person who is not a dependent child anchors exactly one unit unless they join a partner's unit
a co-resident partner (partner_person_id, a symmetric pointer) joins the adult's unit; partners always share a unit

a dependent child joins the unit of its co-resident parent parent_1_person_id; a lone co-resident parent is always parent 1 (the parent_1_person_id pointer definition in microcosm.frame.concepts; the pointer checks flag parent_2_person_id without parent_1_person_id as parent_order, microcosm.frame.concepts._check_pointers), so parent_2_person_id never chooses the unit
every other adult in the household, including boarders and flatmates, forms their own unit

dependent_child.candidate_basis: UNVERIFIED proposal. The Social Security Act 2018 definitions of "child" and "dependent child" were not read in this lane. The hub confirms the statutory text before D1; the CREATE kernel must refuse a null age_limit_years.
dependent_child.rulespec_encoding: None at rulespec-nz 8dc2507: nz/statutes/common/relationships.yaml has status deferred and rules: [], and main_benefits/entitlement.yaml encodes only sole_parent_dependent_child_age_limit for the sole-parent test. When rulespec-nz encodes the definition, the CREATE kernel is to read it from there and this block is to be deleted.

child_without_coresident_parent.status: proposed default for D1; the kernel is to refuse when the reference person is themselves a dependent child

refusals: a unit whose members span two households
a parent or partner pointer to a person outside the household
a dependent child in a household with no adult
open_cases: a person under the age limit who has a co-resident child of their own (teen parent): adult or dependent child is a D1 call
a child whose two co-resident parents are not partners: the rule above places the child with parent 1
invariants: every person is in exactly one unit
every unit has at least one adult
every dependent child shares a unit with a parent or the reference person
sum of family weights equals the sum over households of household weight times units in the household

unit_attributes.note: Unit attributes the planned unit-attributes node (transport.unit_attributes@1, package G5a) is to emit on the family entity, for the reg 17/18 bridge and the group encode to read. The bridge's adults_in_couple multiplier (as_rate_bridge.json) is not declared here yet; the bridge kernels (package G7) are to settle it.

columns.family.family_type: category of the MC7 unit: single, couple, sole parent, couple with children
columns.family.n_dependent_children: count of dependent children in the unit
columns.family.is_sole_parent: single adult with at least one dependent child
columns.family.is_partnered: the unit contains a partnered couple
columns.family.is_single: the unit has one adult (not family.is_partnered)
columns.family.youngest_dependent_child_age: age of the youngest dependent child; 0 when there is none
